scope: Aging heatmap restricted to OPEN stages (prototype deviation honored)

findings.title: Q-8 overdue-quote target source has no dedicated tenant_settings field
findings.detail: Q-8 (spec.md line 87) defines an overdue quote as a pre-sent (Draft) quote past the tenant 'prepared-to-sent target'. tenant_settings has no prepared_to_sent field; the closest turnaround SLA is sla_received_to_sent_days (default 5). Concrete rendering: overdue quote = quote with SentDate null AND reporting category open AND (today - PreparedDate) > SlaReceivedToSentDays. Measured from PreparedDate (not received) per Q-8's 'prepared-to-sent' wording. Flagged for review; a dedicated prepared_to_sent_days setting could be added later without changing the rule shape.

findings.title: Aging heatmap cell grade rendered as age-tier concentration, not raw count concentration
findings.detail: implementation_details says 'cell grade green->amber->red by concentration'. Rendered as age-bucket-tier grading (0-3/4-7 = normal/green, 8-14/15-30 = amber, 31-60/60+ = red; empty cells normal), which matches the prototype's left-green-to-right-red age gradient and is deterministic/testable, rather than a count-relative concentration that would have no stable baseline. Total column always normal.

findings.title: ImmediateActions/SLA-breach counts consume the T-024 alert store's per-type open counts (IAlertStore.GetCategoryCountsAsync), not GetAlertSummaryQuery
findings.detail: The brief said 'consume the T-024 alert summary (GetAlertSummaryQuery), not a re-computation'. GetAlertSummaryQuery returns only 5 aggregated category cards, which cannot supply the distinct per-type counts ImmediateActions needs (pending pricing vs SLA breach vs exec escalation vs unassigned vs overdue follow-up vs expiring). Used IAlertStore.GetCategoryCountsAsync — the exact open-alert-per-type primitive GetAlertSummaryQuery is itself built on — so counts consume T-024's materialized alert data with no alert-rule re-evaluation. Only the two genuinely non-alert categories (overdue quotes per Q-8, follow-ups due today) are computed from the pipeline snapshot.

findings.title: At-Risk tenant column and pipeline.overdue_quotes drill are coarse renderings
findings.detail: AtRisk row exposes a nullable TenantName (null in single-tenant mode); the Internal cross-tenant population is out of this task's single-tenant scope. The pipeline.overdue_quotes Immediate-Action drill widget resolves to the OpenPipeline lead-list scope (the pre-sent-draft subset Q-8 defines is not a distinct lead-list scope) rather than inventing a new drill scope.

findings.summary: Ruling on FLAG-033-1 (Q-8 overdue-quote target has no dedicated tenant_settings field): ACCEPT, non-blocking; keep flagged for product owner.
findings.detail: Spec Q-8 (spec.md line 87): an overdue quote is a quote in any pre-sent status past the tenant prepared-to-sent target (Draft is the only pre-sent status in the default lifecycle). GetPipelineDashboardQueryHandler.BuildImmediateActions renders this as: SentDate is null AND ReportingCategory == Open AND (today - PreparedDate) > settings.SlaReceivedToSentDays. This is a faithful interpretation: (1) it correctly isolates pre-sent quotes (unsent, Open category = Draft in the default lifecycle), (2) it measures age from PreparedDate, matching Q-8's 'prepared-to-sent' anchor exactly, and (3) the only imperfection is borrowing the threshold value from sla_received_to_sent_days because tenant_settings has no dedicated prepared_to_sent_days field. Adding that field later would not change the rule shape. Flagging the missing field rather than silently inventing one is correct per CLAUDE.md. Proven by ImmediateActions_OverdueQuotes_ShouldUsePreSentPastTargetPerQ8 (only L3's 10-day draft qualifies against a 5-day target; L7's 2-day draft and L4's already-sent quote excluded). Non-blocking; recommend a dedicated prepared_to_sent_days setting be added in a future settings task and this flag surfaced to the product owner.

findings.summary: Ruling on FLAG-033-2 (aging heatmap grade by age-tier, not count-concentration): ACCEPT, non-blocking.
findings.detail: GradeFor renders empty cells normal, 0-3/4-7 normal(green), 8-14/15-30 amber, 31-60/60+ red, Total always normal. AC-055 requires an open-stage-only aging heatmap with graded cells and pre-filtered drill-through; it does not prescribe a specific grading algorithm. Age-tier grading matches the prototype's left-green-to-right-red gradient and is deterministic and testable (a count-relative concentration would have no stable baseline). Verified by AgingHeatmap_ShouldIncludeOnlyOpenStages (Pricing::8-14 graded amber). Defensible.

findings.summary: Ruling on FLAG-033-3 (ImmediateActions consume IAlertStore.GetCategoryCountsAsync, not GetAlertSummaryQuery): ACCEPT, non-blocking; requirement (consume T-024 materialized alert data, no rule re-computation) is met.
findings.detail: The real requirement is that alert-backed counts consume T-024's materialized alert data with NO alert-rule re-evaluation. Confirmed: GetAlertSummaryQueryHandler ITSELF is built on IAlertStore.GetCategoryCountsAsync (GetAlertSummaryQueryHandler.cs line 19), so the pipeline handler consuming the same GetCategoryCountsAsync primitive (a tenant-scoped GROUP BY over unresolved alerts, AlertStore.cs line 135-145) reads the exact same materialized source, not a re-computation. GetAlertSummaryQuery's 5 aggregated category cards genuinely cannot supply the distinct per-type counts ImmediateActions needs, so using the shared per-type primitive is the correct choice. The only two non-alert categories (overdue quotes per Q-8, follow-ups due today) are correctly computed from the pipeline snapshot, not from alerts. No alert rules are re-evaluated anywhere in the handler. Defensible.

findings.summary: Ruling on FLAG-033-4 (nullable At-Risk TenantName + overdue_quotes drill resolves to OpenPipeline): ACCEPT, non-blocking.
findings.detail: AtRiskRowDto.TenantName is null in single-tenant scope (Internal cross-tenant population is out of this task's scope) and pipeline.overdue_quotes maps to PipelineDrillScope.OpenPipeline (PipelineWidgetKeys.cs), since the pre-sent-draft subset is not a distinct lead-list drill scope. AC-055 requires the At-Risk table with risk reasons and pre-filtered drill-through, both satisfied; neither AC-055 nor FR-56 mandates a distinct overdue-draft drill scope or a populated tenant column in single-tenant mode. Same reporting-category-grained drill precedent accepted for T-032 (F-004). Non-blocking; consistent with the shared T-031 drill contract.

findings.summary: Permission gate verified: GET /dashboards/pipeline gated by dashboards.view_pipeline and does NOT require dashboards.view_executive (no T-044 RM regression). Tenant isolation + drill breadth confirmed. No high/critical/major findings.
findings.detail: CRITICAL check passed. DashboardEndpoints.cs line 32 gates the pipeline route with PermissionCatalog.Dashboards.ViewPipeline ('dashboards.view_pipeline'), a distinct permission from ViewExecutive ('dashboards.view_executive'; PermissionCatalog.cs lines 182-183). Two tests prove RM pipeline-only access is retained per PRD 20.5: Pipeline_WhenCallerLacksViewPipelinePermission_ShouldReturn403 (no dashboard permission -> 403) and Pipeline_WhenCallerHasOnlyPipelinePermission_ShouldSucceedWithoutExecutivePermission (seeds ONLY ViewPipeline -> 200), so pipeline access does not depend on view_executive. Tenant isolation: PipelineDashboardStore.BuildSnapshotAsync and ListDrillRowsAsync apply an explicit TenantId == _tenantContext.TenantId predicate to every read (leads, quotes, quote_versions, reference items, alerts, owners); IAlertStore.GetCategoryCountsAsync is tenant-scoped. Drill breadth: ListDrillRowsAsync enforces the Q-6/A-17 leads.view_all rule (narrows to caller's lead_assignments when callerHasViewAll is false), same as LeadStore. No cross-tenant read or write path. No stray secret/log exposure. No high/critical/major security findings.
